ev.q: The Data Foundation COVID Impact Survey collected nationally representative data on reported mitigation behaviors during April–June 2020
In April, 78% of adults aged ≥18 years reported wearing a mask
Reported use of face masks increased from 78% in April, to 83% in May, and reached 89% in June
At each time point, >40% of all adults aged ≥18 years reported all six assessed mitigation behaviors
Across all survey waves, reported prevalences of mitigation behaviors were highest among adults aged ≥60 years and lowest among those aged 18–29 years
Among adults who reported face mask use at each time point, a significantly higher percentage reported other mitigation behaviors
The COVID Impact Survey collected data to provide national estimates of health, economic, and social well-being of U.S. adults
Surveys were conducted in three waves (April 20–26, May 4–10, and May 30–June 8)
Test for trend for overall change over time: p-value <0.001.

methods_quotes.q: Pearson’s Chi-squared test was used to assess differences in reported behaviors (individual and cumulative) by age, within each survey wave
Logistic regression models were used to test statistical significance of time trends by assigning calendar week
an iterative raking process was used to adjust for nonresponse, noncoverage, and under- and oversampling
with survey weights applied during analyses for nationally representative estimates
Chi-square p-value <0.05 for differences across age groups, by survey wave.
